rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a conformal Ni coating on W particles before sintering, whereas the paper uses liquid-metal dealloying of a WTaVTi RHEA precursor in molten Cu to create a bicontinuous composite. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis uses spark-plasma sintering at 900–1000 °C and simulated fusion conditions, while the paper uses vacuum-sealed immersion in molten Cu at 1200 °C for 96 h and measures thermal conductivity up to 800 °C with 25 keV He+ irradiation. The processing routes and test conditions are entirely different.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes a Ni interlayer promoting wetting and interdiffusion to reduce voids, whereas the paper's mechanism relies on selective Ti dissolution from interdendritic channels, W-rich passivating interlayer formation, and aligned Cu channels for conductivity. These are different classes of mechanism.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts improved thermal conductivity and mechanical durability relative to uncoated W–Cu composites, while the paper predicts and measures a specific thermal conductivity increase surpassing pure W above 650 °C and reduced He-induced swelling relative to pure W. The predicted properties and comparisons differ.
